record.paper_title: Kontsevich Graphs Act on Nambu-Poisson Brackets, VI. Open Problems
record.original_question: For the vanishing one-vector Nambu micro-graphs that are needed in the dimensional shift d -> d + 1, do all indispensable examples come from descendants of an underlying vanishing set already present over R^{d-1}, rather than from new vanishing micro-graphs whose vanishing mechanisms first appear in the higher dimension?

evidence.quote: Do these indispensable (cf. [6]) vanishing micro-graphs stem only from the underlying vanishing set in Rd−1 through their descendants ?
there appear no new (starting to work) mechanisms of φ(Γd+1) = 0 w.r.t. φ(Γd) = 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider the Kontsevich graph calculus specialised to Nambu–Poisson brackets on R^d, where a Nambu–Poisson bracket is given by the Jacobian determinant of d-1 Casimir functions with respect to the standard volume form. Within this calculus one works with "micro-graphs" Γ_d: oriented graphs whose internal vertices carry copies of a Nambu–Poisson structure expanded in terms of its Casimirs, with one external sink, and whose associated differential-polynomial formula φ(Γ_d) is a (multi-)vector field on R^d. A micro-graph Γ_d is called vanishing in dimension d if φ(Γ_d) ≡ 0 identically on R^d.

A natural lifting (descent) procedure produces, from any micro-graph Γ_d defined over R^d, a collection of descendants over R^{d+1}, obtained by inserting an additional Casimir into each Nambu vertex. A vanishing micro-graph Γ_{d+1} over R^{d+1} is called indispensable if removing it (and its orbit under graph symmetries) destroys the existence of a graph-level solution to the relevant cocycle/coboundary equation in dimension d+1, while its presence is required to balance non-vanishing contributions of other descendants.

Question. For the dimensional shift R^d → R^{d+1}, is it the case that every indispensable vanishing one-vector Nambu micro-graph in dimension d+1 arises as a descendant of some vanishing micro-graph already present over R^d? Equivalently, prove or disprove that no indispensable vanishing micro-graph over R^{d+1} has a vanishing mechanism (e.g., a non-trivial automorphism enforcing φ ≡ 0) that first appears strictly in dimension d+1 and is not inherited from a vanishing micro-graph over R^d via the descent operation.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the most recent installment (2025) of an ongoing series on Kontsevich graphs acting on Nambu–Poisson brackets. Companion papers (parts III–V, 2024–2025) and related theses establish the indispensable role of vanishing micro-graphs in dimensional lifts but do not resolve whether all such indispensable vanishers descend from lower-dimensional vanishing sets. No resolution was located.

status_evidence.title: Kontsevich graphs act on Nambu–Poisson brackets, IV. When the invisible becomes crucial
status_evidence.snippet: There can be no solution in higher dimension without invisible graphs that vanish in d=3 but whose descendants do not all vanish over d=4.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes indispensability of vanishing micro-graphs but does not classify their origin.

status_evidence.title: Kontsevich (micro-)graph invariants in the geometry of Nambu-Poisson brackets
status_evidence.snippet: Thesis on micro-graph invariants and constraints in Nambu-Poisson geometry.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on vanishing mechanisms; problem remains open.
